breadcrumb: Std 8 Science (English) — Unit 18: Organisation of Life — Boxed notes (தெரிந்து தெளிவோம் / Do you know)

questions.quote: Organisms like bacteria, cyanobacteria and mycoplasma, in which the true nucleus is absent, are called prokaryotes. Plants and animals have cells with a well-defined nucleus covered by membrane - eukaryotes. Yeasts and amoeba are unicellular organisms.

en.q: Organisation of Life: Which of the following is a unicellular organism?
en.explanation: Plants, animals and human beings are multicellular.

ta.explanation: தாவரங்கள், விலங்குகள், மனிதர் பல செல் உயிரிகள்.

questions.quote: The average cell size varies from 0.5 to 20 µm in diameter. The cells of bacteria are the smallest in size (1-2 µm). In human body, the smallest cell is red blood cells (7 µm in diameter) and the longest one is the nerve cell which reaches a length of about 90-100 cm. Human egg (ovum) is 100 µm in size. Mycoplasma with a diameter of 0.0001 mm is the smallest bacterium.

en.q: The smallest cell in the human body is the ______.
en.explanation: The longest cell is the nerve cell (90-100 cm); the human ovum is 100 µm.

ta.explanation: மிக நீளமான செல் நரம்புச் செல் (90-100 செ.மீ); மனித முட்டை 100 µm.

questions.quote: Cell is the structural and functional unit of life. Our body is developed from a single cell called zygote. The zygote undergoes continuous mitotic division and forms the foetus. Foetal cells gradually attain change in structure and function: cell differentiation.

en.q: Our body develops from a single cell called the ______.
en.explanation: The zygote divides repeatedly by mitosis to form the foetus.

ta.q: நம் உடல் ______ எனும் ஒற்றைச் செல்லிலிருந்து வளர்ச்சியடைகிறது.
ta.explanation: கருமுட்டை தொடர்ந்து மைட்டாசிஸ் முறையில் பிரிந்து கருவாகிறது.

questions.quote: Tissues are groups of cells that have a similar structure and act together to perform a specific function. They are of two types: simple tissues and complex tissues. Simple tissues are made up of cells of the same type (homogeneous). Complex tissues are made up of different kinds of tissues (heterogeneous).

en.q: A tissue made up of cells of the same kind, like glandular tissue, is a ______ tissue.
en.explanation: Complex tissues, like those of dry skin, are heterogeneous.

ta.q: சுரப்பித் திசு போன்று ஒரே வகைச் செல்களாலான திசு ______ திசு எனப்படும்.
ta.explanation: உலர் தோலின் திசுக்கள் போன்ற சிக்கலான திசுக்கள் பல்வகையானவை.

questions.quote: Four types of tissues: Epithelial (covering) tissue for protection; Muscular (contractile) tissue for movements and locomotion; Connective (supporting) tissue for binding different structures of body; Nervous tissue for conduction of nerve impulses.

en.q: Which tissue is responsible for movements and locomotion?
en.explanation: Muscular tissue is contractile.

ta.explanation: தசைத் திசு சுருங்கும் தன்மை உடையது.

questions.quote: Organs are structures made up of two or more types of tissues, organized to carry out a particular function. Example: brain, heart, lungs, kidneys, liver. Most organs are made up of four types of tissues, for example the intestine.

en.q: An organ is made up of ______.
options: two or more types of tissues organized to carry out a particular function
en.explanation: Examples: brain, heart, lungs, kidneys and liver.

options: ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட செயலைச் செய்ய ஒருங்கிணைக்கப்பட்ட இரண்டு அல்லது அதற்கு மேற்பட்ட திசுக்களால்
ta.explanation: எ.கா: மூளை, இதயம், நுரையீரல், சிறுநீரகம், கல்லீரல்.

questions.quote: The human eye can differentiate approximately 10-12 million colors. Sclera: tough and thick white sheath. Conjunctiva: thin transparent membrane that keeps the eyes moist and clear by secreting small amounts of mucus and tears. Cornea: transparent layer that refracts light. Iris: pigmented layer that controls the size of the pupil. Pupil: small opening at the middle of the iris.

en.q: The coloured portion of the eye, which controls the size of the pupil, is the ______.
en.explanation: The pupil is the small opening at the middle of the iris that allows light to come in.

ta.q: கண்மணியின் அளவைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தும், கண்ணின் நிறமுள்ள பகுதி ______.
ta.explanation: கண்மணி (பியூபில்) கருவிழியின் நடுவிலுள்ள சிறு துளை; அது ஒளியை உள்ளே அனுமதிக்கிறது.

questions.quote: Lens: a transparent, biconvex and adjustable part of an eye, made up of protein. Retina: the layer at the back of the eye where all the images are formed; converts light rays into impulses and sends them to the brain through the optic nerve. Aqueous humour is a watery fluid between the lens and the cornea responsible for the nourishment of both the lens and the cornea.

en.q: The layer at the back of the eye where images are formed is the ______.
en.explanation: The retina converts light rays into impulses and sends signals to the brain through the optic nerve.

ta.explanation: விழித்திரை ஒளிக்கதிர்களைத் தூண்டல்களாக மாற்றிப் பார்வை நரம்பு வழியே மூளைக்கு அனுப்புகிறது.

questions.quote: The inner surface of the nasal cavity is lined with cilia and mucous producing cells, which make it sticky and moist. The cilia and mucous trap dust and germs. The blood vessels in the nose help to warm the inhaled air.

en.q: Dust and germs in inhaled air are trapped in the nose by ______.
en.explanation: Blood vessels in the nose warm the inhaled air.

ta.q: உள்ளிழுக்கும் காற்றிலுள்ள தூசு, நுண்ணுயிரிகளை மூக்கில் தடுத்து நிறுத்துபவை ______.
ta.explanation: மூக்கிலுள்ள இரத்தக் குழாய்கள் உள்ளிழுக்கும் காற்றைச் சூடாக்குகின்றன.

questions.quote: The trachea or windpipe is an elastic tube. Between the pharynx and the trachea lies the larynx commonly known as the voice box. The trachea divides into two bronchi. Each bronchus leads to a lung, where it divides to form bronchioles. Each bronchiole leads to a bunch of air sacs called alveoli.

en.q: The trachea divides into two branches called ______.
en.explanation: Each bronchus leads to a lung and divides and redivides to form bronchioles.

ta.q: மூச்சுக்குழல் (டிரக்கியா) இரு கிளைகளாகப் பிரிகிறது; அவை ______ எனப்படும்.
ta.explanation: ஒவ்வொரு மூச்சுக்கிளையும் ஒரு நுரையீரலுக்குச் சென்று மீண்டும் மீண்டும் பிரிந்து மூச்சுக்கிளைக் குழல்களாகிறது.

questions.quote: The oxygen content in the inhaled air in alveoli is more than the blood flowing through the capillaries. So, the oxygen moves into the blood by simple diffusion. Haemoglobin in the blood combines with oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin. Carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood to the air in the alveoli.

en.q: Haemoglobin combines with oxygen to form ______.
en.explanation: Oxygen enters the blood by simple diffusion.

ta.explanation: ஆக்சிஜன் எளிய விரவலால் இரத்தத்தில் கலக்கிறது.

questions.quote: During inspiration, the sternum is pushed up and outward and the diaphragm is pulled down. This increases the volume of the thoracic cavity and thus the pressure decreases, so air flows into the lungs. During exhalation the diaphragm relaxes, moving higher into the thoracic cavity; the volume decreases and air rushes out. Exhalation is a passive event.

en.q: During inhalation, the diaphragm ______ and the volume of the thoracic cavity ______.
en.explanation: During exhalation the diaphragm relaxes and moves up; the volume of the thoracic cavity decreases.

ta.explanation: வெளிவிடும்போது உதரவிதானம் தளர்ந்து மேலேறும்; மார்புக்குழியின் பருமன் குறையும்.

questions.quote: Homeostasis is a property of the biological system where the self-regulating process tends to maintain the balance for survival. Mammals are capable of maintaining constant body temperature despite changes in the external temperature. The control of blood glucose level: insulin is secreted whenever the blood glucose level rises and glucagon whenever it reduces.

en.q: Insulin is secreted when the blood glucose level ______.
en.explanation: Glucagon is secreted whenever the blood glucose level reduces.

ta.explanation: குளுக்கோஸ் அளவு குறையும்போது குளூகோகான் சுரக்கப்படுகிறது.

questions.quote: Diffusion is the movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to lower concentration. Examples: perfume filling a whole room, the movement of small molecules across a cell membrane, a drop of ink in water, tea powder particles dispersing in hot water, exchange of respiratory gases.

en.q: Which of the following is an example of diffusion?
options: Water moving through a semipermeable membrane into a concentrated solution
Perfume spreading through a whole room
Blood being pumped by the heart
Air flowing into the lungs due to a pressure difference
en.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of solvent across a semipermeable membrane.

options: நீர் ஒரு பகுதி ஊடுருவு சவ்வு வழியே அடர் கரைசலுக்குச் செல்லுதல்
ta.explanation: சவ்வூடுபரவல் என்பது பகுதி ஊடுருவு சவ்வு வழியே கரைப்பான் நகர்வது.

questions.quote: Isotonic: concentration of external and internal solution of the organism are the same. Hypotonic: external solution concentration is less than that of the inner solution; water will rush into the organism. Hypertonic: external solution concentration is greater than the inner solution; water will rush out of the organism.

en.q: In a hypertonic external solution, water ______ the cell.
en.explanation: In a hypotonic external solution water rushes into the cell.

ta.explanation: ஹைப்போடானிக் வெளிக்கரைசலில் நீர் செல்லுக்குள் பாயும்.

questions.quote: The term osmoregulation was coined by Hober in 1902. Osmoregulation is the process by which an organism regulates the water balance in its body and maintains the homeostasis of the body. Organisms are divided into osmoconformers and osmoregulators.

en.q: The term 'osmoregulation' was coined in 1902 by ______.
en.explanation: It is the process of regulating the water balance in the body.

ta.explanation: இது உடலின் நீர்ச் சமநிலையைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தும் செயல்.

questions.quote: Cellular respiration is the process by which organisms break down glucose into a form that the cell can use as energy: ATP. It takes place in the cytoplasm and mitochondria of the cells. Aerobic respiration: Glucose + Oxygen → Carbon dioxide + Water + Energy. Anaerobic respiration occurs in organisms like yeast: glucose → ethanol + CO₂ + energy.

en.q: Energy released during cellular respiration is made available to living cells in the form of ______.
en.explanation: Cellular respiration takes place in the cytoplasm and mitochondria.

ta.q: செல் சுவாசத்தில் வெளியாகும் ஆற்றல் உயிர்ச் செல்களுக்கு ______ வடிவில் கிடைக்கிறது.
ta.explanation: செல் சுவாசம் சைட்டோபிளாசத்திலும் மைட்டோகாண்டிரியாவிலும் நிகழ்கிறது.

questions.quote: Aerobic respiration releases 19 times more energy than anaerobic respiration from the same amount of glucose. In aerobic respiration each glucose molecule produces 36 ATPs.

en.q: In aerobic respiration, each glucose molecule produces ______ ATPs.
en.explanation: Aerobic respiration releases 19 times more energy than anaerobic respiration.

ta.q: காற்று சுவாசத்தில் ஒவ்வொரு குளுக்கோஸ் மூலக்கூறும் ______ ATP-களை உருவாக்குகிறது.
ta.explanation: காற்றிலா சுவாசத்தைவிட 19 மடங்கு அதிக ஆற்றல் வெளியாகிறது.

questions.quote: Metabolism consists of anabolism (the build-up of substances) and catabolism (the breakdown of substances). Anabolism or constructive metabolism supports the growth of new cells; small molecules are changed into larger, more complex molecules. Catabolism or destructive metabolism produces the energy required for all activity in the cells.

en.q: The build-up of substances in the body (constructive metabolism) is called ______.
en.explanation: Catabolism is the breakdown of substances that releases energy.

ta.q: உடலில் பொருள்களை உருவாக்கும் (ஆக்க) வளர்சிதை மாற்றம் ______ எனப்படும்.
ta.explanation: சிதை மாற்றம் பொருள்களைச் சிதைத்து ஆற்றலை வெளியிடுகிறது.

questions.quote: Basal metabolism refers to the minimum energy required to maintain the normal activities of the body during complete rest in a warm atmosphere, 12-18 hours after the intake of food.

en.q: Basal metabolism is the ______ energy required to maintain the normal activities of the body during complete rest.
en.explanation: It is measured in a warm atmosphere, 12-18 hours after food intake.

ta.q: அடிப்படை வளர்சிதை மாற்றம் என்பது முழு ஓய்வில் உடலின் இயல்புச் செயல்களைப் பேணத் தேவையான ______ ஆற்றல்.
ta.explanation: இது வெப்பமான சூழலில், உணவு உட்கொண்ட 12-18 மணி நேரத்திற்குப் பின் கணக்கிடப்படுகிறது.
